answer: Admission requires agents to join a synchronized ceremony where each must anchor 1,000 unique keys to a cryptographic terrace; this ensures that each node maintains a distinct path to the ledger. A verifier monitors the registry for overlapping proofs of identity, and any hollow sign of multiple registration triggers a permanent lock. An honest participant pays one unit for entry, while 1,000 fakes incur a massive audit penalty that hits its nadir only after total expulsion. Credentials expire every 90 days, requiring fresh proof without refund to prevent the re-use of old identities.
